encounters.cc: Six-month history of progressively worsening diarrhea with blood and mucus, occurring 6-8 times daily with nocturnal symptoms, associated with 5 kg weight loss and fatigue.

lines: Six-month history of progressively worsening diarrhea with blood and mucus, occurring 6-8 times daily with nocturnal symptoms, associated with 5 kg weight loss and fatigue.
He reports that his bowel movements are loose, occur 6–8 times daily, and are often accompanied by blood and mucus.
The diarrhea sometimes wakes him at night.
Over the past 3 months, he has lost 5 kg (11 lb) without trying.
He has also noticed occasional low-grade fevers, fatigue, and decreased appetite.
He denies recent travel, antibiotic use, or contact with anyone with similar symptoms.
He has no history of camping, consumption of untreated water, or recent foreign travel.
- HIV infection with AIDS (CDC Stage 3, poorly controlled due to non-adherence)
- History of severe thermal burns (40% total body surface area)
- Split-thickness skin grafting for thermal burn wound coverage
- Tracheostomy (placed during burn admission, subsequently decannulated)
His only medication is a daily multivitamin.
- Bictegravir/Tenofovir alafenamide/Emtricitabine (Biktarvy) 50mg/25mg/200mg PO daily (prescribed; patient reports intermittent adherence)
He has no known drug allergies.
His father has a history of an “intestinal problem” that required surgery in his 40s, but the details are unclear.
He does not smoke or drink alcohol and works as a software engineer.
On review of systems, the patient reports occasional joint pain in his knees and ankles, especially in the morning, which improves throughout the day.
He also describes redness and mild discomfort in his eyes over the past few weeks.
He denies skin rashes, oral ulcers, or chronic back pain.
Temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F), blood pressure 118/74 mm Hg, pulse 84/min, respirations 14/min.
On examination, the patient appears mildly pale but is in no acute distress.
His abdomen is soft with mild tenderness in the lower quadrants, without rebound or guarding.
There is no palpable hepatosplenomegaly or abdominal masses.
Bowel sounds are present and normoactive.
Rectal examination reveals gross blood mixed with stool.
No perianal fistulas or abscesses are noted.
Initial laboratory studies show mild normocytic anemia and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate.
Stool cultures and ova/parasite studies are negative.

lines: Two-week progressive weakness in left arm, difficulty walking, mild headache, and personality changes noted by partner; denies fever or neck stiffness.

This 37-year-old male with HIV/AIDS (CDC Stage 3, poorly controlled), prior progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, and cryptococcal meningitis presents to the clinic with a 2-week history of progressive weakness in his left arm and difficulty walking.
He reports a mild headache but denies fever, neck stiffness, or photophobia.
His partner mentions that he has been increasingly forgetful and had a personality change.
His antiretroviral therapy has been irregular due to social circumstances.

His CD4 count is 150/mm3 and viral load is elevated.
MRI of the brain shows multiple nonenhancing white matter lesions without mass effect or edema.

lines: Two-week odynophagia, dysphagia, and retrosternal chest pain with 5 kg weight loss; failed one-week fluconazole trial for presumed candidiasis.

This 38-year-old male with HIV infection with AIDS, ulcerative colitis, and history of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, cryptococcal meningitis, and miliary tuberculosis, presents with persistent symptoms.
His antiretroviral therapy has been irregular due to social circumstances.
He reports a recent weight loss of 5 kg and has a low-grade fever.
Despite treatment with oral fluconazole for one week, his symptoms have not improved.
He denies any vesicular lesions in the oropharynx.
